heading: Understand your rights (Welsh version)
contents.title: Contents
section.main.heading: Special measures
section.main.intro: If you are giving evidence as a victim, you have the right to request special measures to ensure you give your best evidence during your court hearing.
section.whoMightGet.heading: Who might get special measures
section.whoMightGet.p1: Special measures are not for everybody but there are certain circumstances where you might qualify for the extra help this offers.
section.whoMightGet.p2: For example, if the court considers you vulnerable, such as a person under 18, or you have mental or physical needs in court.
section.whoMightGet.p3: If the court considers you are at risk of being intimidated while in court, this may also be good reason to get special measures.
section.whoMightGet.p4: This could include victims of sexual abuse or domestic violence, a crime involving a knife or a gun or victims of modern slavery.
section.whatHelp.heading: What help could be available
section.whatHelp.p1: Depending on the circumstances, victims could get a range of help while in court.
section.whatHelp.p2: This could include giving evidence behind a screen, or by remote link from another court building or police station.
section.whatHelp.p3: Pre-recording a witness statement could also be a special measure to be considered.
section.whatHelp.p4: For those who are worried about attending court, pre-trial visits can also be offered – these allow witnesses to tour a court room and understand how a trial will be held.
section.whatHelp.p5: Intermediaries – a person who attends court with you throughout as support - are also an option.
section.howToRequest.heading: How to request special measures
section.howToRequest.p1: When a crime is reported, the police will do a victim needs assessment for the investigation to see if you need any support – this may include getting an interpreter to help give a statement.
section.howToRequest.p2: A police witness care officer will carry out a second assessment to ensure a victim is prepared to give evidence in court.
section.howToRequest.p3: If you are legally vulnerable or intimidated, the police, or someone from the police witness care unit, will explain what special measures are and how they work, answering your questions. Together, you will decide what you want to ask for or if you want any special measures at all.
section.howToRequest.p4: A judge or magistrate will consider your case and whether your circumstances mean you will get any special measures.
